Arrays.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element at a given index in a 1D array?
Arrays.explanation: Arrays provide constant time O(1) random access because the memory address is computed directly: Base Address + (Index × Element Size).

Arrays.question: In C programming, how is array indexing zero-based represented in memory?
options: arr[i] is internally evaluated as *(arr + i)
Array elements are dynamically scattered in heap memory
Arrays.explanation: In C, arr[i] is syntactically equivalent to *(arr + i). Since the offset from the base address of the 0th element is 0, indexing begins at 0.

Arrays.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting an element at the beginning of an array of size n?
Arrays.explanation: Inserting at the beginning requires shifting all n existing elements one position to the right, taking O(n) time.

Arrays.question: What happens if you access an index beyond the declared size of an array in C (e.g. arr[10] for int arr[5])?
options: A compile-time syntax error is raised
The array automatically doubles its capacity
Arrays.explanation: C does not perform runtime array bounds checking. Accessing out-of-bounds indices leads to undefined behavior or segmentation fault.

Stack.question: Which data structure principle does a Stack strictly follow?
Stack.explanation: A stack follows Last-In First-Out (LIFO), meaning the most recently added item is the first one removed.

Stack.question: What condition represents 'Stack Overflow' in an array-based implementation of capacity MAX?
Stack.explanation: In 0-indexed arrays of size MAX, the highest valid index is MAX - 1. When top == MAX - 1, the stack is full.

Stack.question: Which of the following is NOT a standard application of a Stack?
options: Undo / Redo operation in text editors
Stack.explanation: CPU Round-Robin process scheduling uses a FIFO Queue, not a Stack.

Stack.question: What is the time complexity of the peek() operation on a stack?
Stack.explanation: The peek() operation directly inspects the element at index 'top' without modifying the stack, taking O(1) constant time.

Queue.question: Which order of processing does a standard Queue data structure use?
Queue.explanation: Queues adhere to First-In First-Out (FIFO) — elements are enqueued at the rear and dequeued from the front.

Queue.question: What major limitation of a linear array-based queue does a Circular Queue solve?
options: Eliminates the need for dynamic memory
Prevents the false overflow problem when spaces are freed at the front
Reduces search time from O(n) to O(1)
Queue.explanation: In a linear queue, front moves forward, leaving unused slots at the start. A circular queue wraps rear back to index 0 using modulo arithmetic.

Queue.question: In a Circular Queue of capacity N, what formula gives the next index for the rear pointer?
Queue.explanation: The circular wrap-around uses modulo arithmetic: (rear + 1) % N.

Queue.question: Which graph traversal algorithm primarily uses a Queue data structure?
Queue.explanation: Breadth-First Search (BFS) explores vertices level-by-level using a FIFO queue.

Classes_Objects.question: What is the default access specifier for members of a C++ class if none is specified?
Classes_Objects.explanation: In C++, all members of a class are private by default, whereas in a struct they are public by default.

Classes_Objects.question: Which of the following correctly describes 'Encapsulation' in C++?
options: Allowing multiple functions to share the same name
Bundling data members and methods inside a class while restricting direct access
Deriving new classes from an existing parent class
Dynamically allocating memory with the new keyword
Classes_Objects.explanation: Encapsulation binds data and functions together into a single unit and hides implementation details using private access.

Classes_Objects.question: What is the role of the 'this' pointer in C++?
options: Points to the base class of an object
Points to the next object in memory
An implicit pointer holding the memory address of the invoking object
Classes_Objects.explanation: 'this' is an implicit constant pointer available inside non-static member functions, pointing to the object that invoked the function.

Inheritance_Polymorphism.question: Which keyword is used in C++ base classes to enable dynamic run-time polymorphism for member functions?
Inheritance_Polymorphism.explanation: The 'virtual' keyword instructs the C++ compiler to perform dynamic dispatch via the virtual table (vtable) at runtime.

Inheritance_Polymorphism.question: What is a pure virtual function in C++?
options: A virtual function declared with '= 0' that must be overridden by derived classes
A function that cannot be modified
A static function that accepts no parameters
Inheritance_Polymorphism.explanation: A pure virtual function (e.g., virtual void draw() = 0;) makes the class abstract, meaning it cannot be instantiated directly.

Inheritance_Polymorphism.question: Which form of polymorphism is demonstrated by function overloading in C++?
Inheritance_Polymorphism.explanation: Function and operator overloading are resolved at compile time, known as static or compile-time polymorphism.
